source.title: The Nucleotide Transformer: Building and Evaluating Robust Foundation Models for Human Genomics
source.authors: Hugo Dalla-torre; Liam Gonzalez; Javier Mendoza-Revilla; Nicolas Lopez Carranza; Adam Henryk Grzywaczewski; Francesco Oteri; Christian Dallago; Evan Trop; B. D. de Almeida; Hassan Sirelkhatim; Guillaume Richard; Marcin J. Skwark; Karim Beguir; Marie Lopez; Thomas Pierrot

record.file_problem: No apparent text problem. The supplied text is the full Nature Methods article; the ID is a bioRxiv DOI.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends language-model loss-scaling measurements to DNA masked-language models, reporting training loss as a function of tokens seen. It does not fit or test a power law.
record.gate_note: Figure 5a reports NT-v2 training-loss trajectories against training tokens, so these are recorded as results relevant to the other-modality version. The study does not report held-out pretraining loss, power-law fits, extrapolation from smaller runs, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its downstream benchmarks are not extracted as results for V6: they do not test a predictive relation between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: This DNA foundation-model paper uses Chinchilla-style scaling advice only to set NT-v2 training length ('Inspired by Chinchilla scaling laws'). It does not test any scaling-law version. Fig. 5a plots training loss (not held-out loss) against tokens for four NT-v2 sizes, with no power-law fit, no exponents, no compute axis and no extrapolation. Its scale comparisons are of downstream MCC and are confounded by architecture and dataset changes between NT-v1 and NT-v2. No result bears on whether the power-law form holds in this modality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that larger models consistently improved downstream performance across the 18 tasks. They attribute NT-v2's 10–50x parameter reduction at equal or better MCC to architecture, data and longer training. They make no claim about loss power laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains DNA masked-language models and plots training loss against tokens; it does not use the original studies' held-out-loss fitting, extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies model size and training duration; it also changes architecture between NT-v1 and NT-v2 and uses different pre-training datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: In DNA masked-LM models, downstream MCC rises with model size within NT-v1. Across NT-v2, the 250M model (MCC 0.769) slightly beats 500M only after about 900B tokens. Architecture and data changes let a 50M NT-v2 match the 500M and 1000G 2.5B NT-v1 models (Fig. 5b,c).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In genomic language models, downstream performance gains from parameter scale are small relative to gains from architecture and pre-training data choices, and are not monotonic in size.

record.problems: The loss result is presented as a figure without numerical values or a described power-law fit, and it is training loss rather than held-out loss.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream task benchmark results, including model-size comparisons and NT-v2 downstream performance by training duration (Figs. 2 and 5b,c), were not extracted because the study does not test downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: No held-out language-model loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep. Chinchilla is used only as motivation for longer training.
No loss comparison across shapes at fixed parameter count.
DNA MLM loss curves are shown without any power-law fit or held-out evaluation, so the form is untested.
Downstream MCC is reported by size and tokens, but no predictive relation to scale or loss is tested, and it is confounded by architecture and data changes.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T3' relation is too generous: the loss curves carry no fitted law and cannot bear on the power-law form. Rows are kept linked to V5 as cannot_determine for traceability, but no verdicts are given. The Methods text on NT-v2 token budgets contains an apparent typo ('50M- and 250M' for 300B, then '250M and 500M' for 1T).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is reported.
The study compares architectures and model sizes for downstream tasks, not loss at fixed parameter count across architecture variants.
The study reports DNA-model training-loss curves, but does not fit power laws or test held-out loss, parameter- or compute-scaling, extrapolation, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling.
Downstream task performance is benchmarked, but no predictive relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss is tested.
The study does not compare scaling-law fitting choices, exponents or curve bending.
